prd.oneLiner: Connect seller onboarding, products, inventory, orders, delivery, fee settlement, disputes, policy enforcement, and marketplace outcomes in one operating flow.
prd.goal: Reduce seller onboarding and product-approval lead time while improving visibility into fulfillment, settlement, and policy compliance.
prd.whyNow: Seller data, product review, inventory, fulfillment, fee settlement, and policy violations are separated, making marketplace quality and trust difficult to operate consistently.
prd.problem: Seller data, product review, inventory, fulfillment, fee settlement, and policy violations are separated, making marketplace quality and trust difficult to operate consistently.
prd.solution: Connect seller onboarding, products, inventory, orders, delivery, fee settlement, disputes, policy enforcement, and marketplace outcomes in one operating flow.
prd.alternatives: Email, chat, spreadsheets, and manual ledgers
prd.differentiator: Manage intake, processing, and operations data as one connected source of truth.

targets.name: Marketplace seller listing products and marketplace operator
targets.needs: Quickly register needed work and know its status.
targets.pain: Seller data, product review, inventory, fulfillment, fee settlement, and policy violations are separated, making marketplace quality and trust difficult to operate consistently.

targets.name: Seller operations, policy, and settlement coordinator
targets.needs: Manage priority and history and review operations metrics.
targets.pain: Seller data, product review, inventory, fulfillment, fee settlement, and policy violations are separated, making marketplace quality and trust difficult to operate consistently.

targets.name: System and policy administrator
targets.needs: Manage access, policy, and audit history.
targets.pain: Seller data, product review, inventory, fulfillment, fee settlement, and policy violations are separated, making marketplace quality and trust difficult to operate consistently.

scenarios.text: An operational user registers required work and checks its status.
An operator processes queued work and handles exceptions.
System and policy administrator reviews policy and access.
System and policy administrator reviews audit records and operating metrics.

prd.northStar: Share of operations requests completed on time

kpis.name: On-time processing rate
kpis.target: Reduce seller onboarding and product-approval lead time while improving visibility into fulfillment, settlement, and policy compliance.
kpis.method: Monthly aggregation of state changes against target dates

kpis.name: Operations visibility
kpis.method: Share of records connected to reporting

inScope: Seller application, business details, product, price, inventory, and shipping-policy registration
Seller status, product, inventory, order, delivery, settlement, and policy-violation history lookup
Seller onboarding review, product review, inventory synchronization, order fulfillment, settlement, dispute, and enforcement handling
Seller activity, product approval, order fulfillment, cancellation, settlement, policy violation, and GMV reporting
Seller application, business details, product, price, inventory, and shipping-policy registration validation and duplicate prevention
nonGoals: Replacing adjacent systems such as accounting or payroll
assumptions: User and organization data are available through company SSO.
Operators manage policy and classification criteria.
risks: Weak initial classification can cause incorrect processing.
Stale source data can reduce operational trust.
openQuestions: What defines urgent processing and approval?
What are the post-completion verification and reopen rules?
constraints: State, owner, and priority changes require audit logs.
Permission, policy, and state changes require audit logs.
